literature_notes: All eight ledger lines were evaluated. L1–L5 (PMC7660923) concern mPR constructs assembled for PAQR5/mPRgamma in CHO cells. L2 reports that a C-terminally GFP-tagged construct was detected by anti-GFP immunostaining under non-permeabilized conditions, which the authors interpret as extracellular C-terminus localization. However, the authoritative computed topology for PAQR5 places residues 318–330 (the C-terminal tail) firmly in the INTRACELLULAR compartment. Because the topology landmarks are authoritative for boundary decisions, the C-terminus cannot qualify as an extracellular surface site; it is recorded in other_positions. L3 confirms the N-terminus is intracellular (no non-permeabilized staining for GFP-mPR), consistent with the topology placing residues 1–48 intracellularly. L4 reports that an N-terminal HA tag caused impaired trafficking, further disqualifying the N-terminus. L5 describes the same constructs as L2–L4 and adds no new surface-accessible position. L6–L8 (PMC5507890) explicitly concern mPRbeta (PAQR8), a different PAQR family member; they cannot ground sites for PAQR5. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any of the four extracellular loops (ECL1: 71–81, ECL2: 135–150, ECL3: 203–222, ECL4: 274–294). Because no ledger line supports an extracellular tag insertion for PAQR5, sites = [].

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP (mPR-GFP) was detected by anti-GFP immunostaining under non-permeabilized conditions in CHO cells, which the authors interpret as extracellular; however, the authoritative computed topology places the C-terminal tail (residues 318–330) intracellularly, so this terminus is not a valid extracellular surface-tag site.

N-terminally GFP-tagged mPR (GFP-mPR) showed no staining under non-permeabilized conditions, confirming intracellular localization of the N-terminus, consistent with the authoritative topology placing residues 1–48 intracellularly.
N-terminal HA-tag (HA-mPR) caused impaired trafficking of the full-length construct in CHO cells, making the N-terminus unsuitable even as an intracellular label without further engineering.
